pages.text: Most items contain spirits of several types. The easiest way to harness these spirits is by turning an item into a $(bold)hallow$(): an item that can store and transfer spirits of a specific type. Hallowed items also retain their original functionality.$(br2)A hallow's default spirit capacity is equal to the total number of spirits its base item contains.
As seen in JEI, a redstone block has 18 Tech, 18 Fortune, and 16 Red spirits.

To make a hallow, simply place the desired item in an item focus, influenced by foci containing any power sources (Self or bound mobs). The focus must be above a specific block, which affects the hallow's capacity. Possible blocks are iron (33%), gold (66%), diamond (100%), or netherite (300%). These multipliers also apply to the power cost.$(br2)Items can be un-hallowed with a grindstone.
Hallowing an ender pearl. Notice how it adopts the colors of its spirit type.

pages.title: Determining Spirit Type
pages.text: A hallow's spirit type is chosen randomly from one of the spirit types its base item contains. If the hallow has item influences when created, it will try to choose a spirit type it shares with all those items. The choice will favor non-color spirits if possible.

pages.title: Hallows in Diagrams
pages.text: In item or block foci, hallows will try to extract spirits from their influences. This will destroy normal blocks and items, and drain other hallows.$(br2)Hallows can be "overfilled" over capacity if they break down an item that yields more spirits than they can hold. However, they only absorb half the "extra" spirits.

Many hallows can be placed in the world as blocks. When in block foci, they extract or transfer spirits just like item hallows in item foci.$(br2)You can use a held hallow on a placed hallow to extract spirits from it (hold shift to insert spirits instead).$(br2)When breaking a placed hallow, it will only remain a hallow if the block drops itself.
Most hallows maintain their spirit colors, but some ignore or distort them.
